clue.text: Very easy to understand in the fortune-teller's sphere

definitions.meaning: perfectly plain and transparent in meaning
playfully, describing the glass ball a clairvoyant gazes into

explanation.surface: Something is plainly obvious, or perhaps only visible to a clairvoyant gazing into her glass ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly lucid, and a fortune-teller's ball is literally made of the transparent glass the phrase names.

clue.text: Very comfortable like a carpet-moth?

definitions.meaning: cosy and snug in one's surroundings
literally describing an insect living in a floor covering

explanation.surface: A cosy person is compared to a moth nestling in the pile of a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means thoroughly cosy, and an insect tucked into a floor mat is literally that creature in that place.

clue.text: Left cockney lady at northern town, or even more northerly one

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so 'her' becomes 'er
Wick is a town in the far north of Scotland, in Caithness

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves a London woman in a Highland town and heads further north still.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (working-class Londoners) drop initial H, hence 'ER for 'her'. The definition is a town further north than Wick: the capital of Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland capital lies well north of Wick on the Scottish mainland, so it is a still more northerly town.

clue.text: Opening for a photographer perhaps

parts.note: reads like a job vacancy for someone with a camera, but means the hole in a camera lens that lets light in

explanation.surface: A job advert announces a vacancy for a photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjustable hole in a camera lens controlling incoming light is a technical word for a gap or opening.

clue.text: Namely nice switchback railway

parts.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means namely

indicators.note: a switchback twists back and forth, so the letters of nice are turned about

explanation.surface: Someone praises a pleasant roller-coaster at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switchback' rearranges NICE into ENIC. A scenic railway is an old name for a fairground roller-coaster, so the answer plus 'railway' makes the ride the surface names.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer completes the name of a fairground ride, the scenic railway, a miniature track through painted landscapes.

clue.text: Onlooker, heartless boy, one on his feet

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of boy is removed

parts.note: someone standing upright is a stander

explanation.surface: A spectator is described as a callous lad who stays upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who watches an event without taking part is an onlooker or spectator.

clue.text: Stiff and formal to be precise

definitions.meaning: rigidly correct in manner, like a starched collar

explanation.surface: Someone is described as rigid and correct, or is simply being exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch stiffens linen, so the word figuratively describes prim, formal and fussily correct people.

clue.text: Trees recently stolen from military town

parts.note: alders are trees of the birch family
hot is slang for stolen goods freshly taken

explanation.surface: Some timber has just been pilfered from an army town.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDERSHOT, in Hampshire, is the traditional home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hampshire garrison town has been the home of the British Army since the 1850s.

clue.text: See 1
Measure of mercy

definitions.meaning: a fourth part, as of a pound or a gallon
clemency shown to a defeated enemy

explanation.surface: A fragment about how much mercy can be measured out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourth part is a unit of measure, and sparing a beaten foe is the old military sense of clemency.

clue.text: Nothing included by confused nutter was false

indicators.note: something included by another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
a muddled word has its letters jumbled

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A muddled madman's claim that nothing was in it turned out to be a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges NUTTER, and 'included by' puts O inside: N-O-TTRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is false, a lie or inaccuracy.

clue.text: A kit's replaced in no end of panic for a cricketer perhaps

indicators.note: one piece is set inside another
dropping the end means the last letter of panic goes
items replaced are put back differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kit gets swapped around in a frantic last-minute rush before a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' trims PANIC to PANI; 'replaced' rearranges A KIT'S, and 'in' puts the result after the P. The 's of kit's supplies an S here, standing for 'is' rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakistan is a leading Test cricket nation, so one of its players is an example of a cricketer.

clue.text: Ran up with speed to provide a commentary

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word ran is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A sports broadcaster dashes up quickly to start commentating.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses RAN to NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give a spoken account of events, as a commentator does.

clue.text: Plant in a container accordingly

parts.note: a can is a metal container
thus means accordingly or therefore

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: grow your plant in a pot as directed.
explanation.definitionFit: The bear's breeches is a Mediterranean perennial whose leaves decorate Corinthian columns.

clue.text: He reverses better

definitions.meaning: a person who moves something back, read as back plus -er
one who bets, a punter, read as bet plus -er

explanation.surface: A man who changes his mind is said to be an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions are jokey: 'better' is not the comparative but one who bets. The answer also means a financial supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who backs a horse is a punter who bets, and one who backs a car moves it in reverse.

clue.text: See 2
Apply lotion when mob create havoc

indicators.note: chaos throws the letters of mob create into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone tends their bruises as rioters run amok.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrocate is to rub a liniment into an aching part of the body.

clue.text: Melissa got up to the border town

parts.note: Mel is a short form of the name Melissa
rose means got up from bed or a seat

explanation.surface: Melissa rises and travels to a frontier settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: MELROSE is a town in the Scottish Borders, known for its ruined abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: This town lies in the Scottish Borders region near the frontier with England, famous for its abbey ruins.

clue.text: No credit given by place with money

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
cash is ready money

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper refuses credit and demands payment on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made immediately at the time of purchase, rather than on account, means no credit is extended.

clue.text: Diplomatic case?

parts.note: reads as a matter for diplomats, but describes a slim briefcase that bears the name of an embassy official

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an affair is a matter for diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior embassy official gives his title to a slim hard briefcase, so the word names both.

clue.text: Serviceman (or servicewoman nowadays)?

parts.note: not a soldier but a cleric who conducts church services, a role now open to women too

explanation.surface: A remark on women now joining the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket alludes to the Church of England ordaining women, which began in 1994.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric who leads church services, a role women may now take in the Church of England.

clue.text: As an unbeliever, I fled in confusion

indicators.note: letters in confusion are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A heretic explains that he ran away in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rejects a given religious faith is called an unbeliever.

clue.text: Stabbed a rebel leader in haste

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: speed means haste

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, here of rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel chief was run through in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R (first letter of 'rebel') go inside SPEED: SPE-AR-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with a pointed weapon is to stab.

clue.text: One doesn't care to lose it

definitions.text: One doesn't care to lose it

parts.words: One doesn't care to lose it
parts.note: suggests reluctance, but means that once you stop caring you have lost concern for a thing

explanation.surface: A remark about something no one wants to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Care' looks like 'wish', but the clue means that losing this is what not caring is.
explanation.definitionFit: When you lose concern or curiosity about something, you no longer care about it.

clue.text: She went round city limits with head tribesman for the tool

indicators.note: something going round another surrounds it, so one piece holds the other
a word's limits are its first and last letters, here of city
the head of a word is its first letter, here of tribesman

explanation.surface: A woman circles the city outskirts with the clan chief to fetch an implement.
explanation.walkthrough: C and Y (first and last letters of 'city') plus T (head of 'tribesman') go inside SHE: S-CYT-HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The long curved blade on a pole used to cut grass is a farming tool.

clue.text: Informed in writing by this accountant

definitions.meaning: notified formally by a written document
the kind of qualified accountant called chartered or ... in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone was notified by letter by their accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: A certified accountant is a British professional qualification, alongside chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: To certify is to attest formally on paper, and a certified accountant holds a recognised professional qualification.

clue.text: Any chief involved in lawlessness?

indicators.note: letters involved are entangled together into a new order

parts.note: arch means chief, as in archbishop or arch-enemy

explanation.surface: Asks whether a chief's involvement means a breakdown of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence of government and order is a state of lawlessness.

clue.text: Woman boxer?

parts.note: suggests a female pugilist, but means the mythical woman linked to a famous box of evils

explanation.surface: A question about a female fighter in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth this woman opened a jar (later called a box) releasing all evils into the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The first woman in Greek myth is famous for opening the box that released the world's ills.

clue.text: Disconnect one from Paris with a jerk

parts.note: un is French for one
a hitch is a sudden jerk or tug

explanation.surface: A Parisian is cut loose with a sudden tug.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something hooked or tied, such as a trailer, is to disconnect it.

clue.text: Dish from Mexico and Chile, a crumble

indicators.note: letters crumbled break apart and reform in a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe blends Mexican and Chilean food into a dessert crumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled corn tortilla stuffed and baked under chilli sauce is a classic Mexican dish.
